exposure: Caesarean section due to prolonged labour/dystocia
outcome: Prevalence of caesarean section due to prolonged labour/dystocia
cohort: 817 pregnant women in Kigali and Northern Province, Rwanda
finding: While the prevalence of pregnancy-related complications like pre-eclampsia/eclampsia, postpartum hemorrhage, and cesarean section due to prolonged labor/dystocia was relatively low, the study identified caesarean section as the primary reason for transferring pregnant women from lower to higher-level healthcare facilities.
mod_finding: Caesarean section was the main reason for the transfer of pregnant women from health centres to district hospitals.
